steps.what: Receive prescription or refill request and locate matching patient record
Check prescription request completeness against required administrative fields
Verify request accuracy and resolve missing information or refer uncertainties to pharmacist

tasks.design: Configure required-field checks in {OTHER} pharmacy software for supported electronic requests. Keep identity matching, source accuracy and queries with the technician; a complete request is not a clinically approved prescription.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routine omissions are found by rereading requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can flag absent fields without interpreting clinical intent.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous instructions, wrong patients and information that is present but incorrect.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a plausible request needs clarification rather than completion.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time locating obvious omissions; retain the same verification duties.

reach.task: Resolve requests whose meaning or clinical validity remains uncertain
reach.learn: Which uncertainties must be referred rather than filled in

evidence.claim: Required-field validation can support administrative completeness without establishing clinical accuracy; savings are an unmeasured scenario.
Dutch pharmacy systems use G-Standaard medication surveillance; this is a separate clinical control and does not prove the proposed administrative saving.

assumptions: Boundary is receipt and administrative verification, excluding prescribing, dispensing and pharmacist clinical authorisation.

For electronic requests the prescriber or existing request portal produces request ID, patient identifiers, prescriber identifier, medicine, strength, form, directions, quantity and date during unchanged upstream capture; no new upstream field entry is assumed.
s1 retains technician matching and manual intake time; paper or unstructured requests receive manual completeness checks in s2, with no model interpreting a dose.
The pharmacist defines the local required-field rules during setup; recurring rule clarification is charged to upkeep rather than transferred for free.
Test native configuration before custom work; missing fields are queried, never inferred. Existing surveillance runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Electronic request coverage and available native validation
research_questions: What share of omission checking can native fields remove while source verification time stays unchanged?

already_counted.description: Review flags and manually check unsupported requests in s2

incremental.description: Check validation changes and report rule problems

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+17.5+45=82.5; gross 17.5 minus 1 focal upkeep gives net 16.5. High needs supported electronic requests; low covers paper intake and exceptions consuming the benefit. Pharmacist upkeep is separate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Retrieve prescription source and confirm patient and prescription identifiers
Enter prescription information into pharmacy computer database draft fields
Compare draft with prescription source and approve saving exact database entry

tasks.design: Use the native electronic-prescription import in {OTHER} pharmacy software to populate a draft, when available. The technician checks the exact draft against the source before saving, and manually enters unsupported prescriptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prescription fields are copied between an existing source and the database.
tasks.enabler_now: A supported structured import can preserve field values and source identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Identity errors, unsupported directions and mismatched medicine codes.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a source-to-record discrepancy before it affects later work.
tasks.altitude: Less transcription with the same data-entry accountability.

reach.task: Review clinical issues after technician data entry
reach.learn: Separate faithful transcription from clinical approval

evidence.claim: Structured imports can reduce rekeying when source and destination schemas match; availability and estimated saving require local testing.

assumptions: Boundary is database transcription, not request verification or clinical approval; overlapping work must be allocated once in a role roll-up.

The existing prescribing system produces patient ID, prescription ID/version, prescriber, medicine code, strength, dosage form, directions, quantity and issue date during unchanged prescribing capture.
s1 counts source retrieval and identity confirmation; s2 retains unsupported-source entry and mapping exceptions. No new structured input is demanded from the prescriber.
Use native import first; missing or incompatible fields go to manual entry, with no guessed directions or unattended database save.
s3 retains full source comparison and approves only the exact entry version; any change requires another comparison.
unknowns: Native import support and proportion of sources already imported
research_questions: How much actual rekeying remains after excluding existing automatic import runtime?

already_counted.description: Unsupported input entry and mapping exceptions in s2
Source comparison and save approval in s3

incremental.description: Check import changes and investigate failed mappings

approvals.approved_version: Patient ID plus prescription source version and every database field in the displayed draft; any field or source change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+10+25=60; gross 40 minus 2 focal upkeep gives net 38. High needs compatible sources currently rekeyed; low covers mostly paper or already-imported sources where no new labour benefit remains. Other-role interface time is separate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather patient profile details and current medication sources
Establish or update patient profile and medication list draft
Verify profile changes with sources and save or refer unresolved discrepancies

tasks.design: Configure {OTHER} pharmacy software to reuse existing profile fields and show source-linked changes rather than rewriting a whole list. The technician collects information, checks each change and refers unresolved medication discrepancies without a model deciding which treatment is current.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unchanged profile information is repeatedly entered while differences are hard to see.
tasks.enabler_now: Native edit forms and change views can reduce rewriting without replacing reconciliation.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting sources and medicines a patient takes differently from the record.
tasks.human_edge: Asking useful questions and preserving uncertainty for the pharmacist.
tasks.altitude: Less profile rewriting; no new clinical decision rights.

reach.learn: How to document source uncertainty without selecting a regimen

evidence.claim: Field reuse and source-linked editing can reduce repeated profile entry; the proposed time reduction is model knowledge and needs measurement.

assumptions: Boundary is technician profile maintenance, excluding clinical reconciliation decisions and source-system prescribing.
s1 counts gathering identity, contact details, medication name/code, strength, directions as reported, source, date and uncertainty; no free structured medication list is assumed.
Existing pharmacy records are produced by prior authorised record entry; s2 reuses those fields and manually captures new information from s1.
Test native edit and history views before custom code; absent or conflicting data remains explicit and follows existing referral routes.
s3 checks the exact edited version; new changes invalidate the save approval. No medication is started or stopped by this tool.
unknowns: How much rewriting occurs and which native change views exist
research_questions: Does field reuse save entry time without shortening medication-source checks?

already_counted.description: Manual new-field entry in s2 and profile verification/referrals in s3

incremental.description: Maintain entry layout and inspect source-link problems

approvals.approved_version: Displayed patient ID, all changed profile and medication fields, source dates and unresolved flags; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+14+25=79; gross 21 minus 1 upkeep gives net 20. High assumes substantial repeated fields; low covers mostly new profiles and conflicting sources requiring full manual entry.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inspect drug storage conditions and access security against pharmacy procedures
Maintain proper drug storage and security and refer abnormal conditions

tasks.design: Retain physical storage checks and corrective handling under pharmacy procedures. Existing {OTHER} environmental-monitoring software can remain in use, but its current runtime does not remove the technician's physical checks or security duties.
tasks.previous_blocker: A digital reading does not establish correct placement, access control or physical condition.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional reliable producer has been established to replace direct checks.
tasks.still_hard: Responding appropriately to uncertain exposure and security problems.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing conditions a sensor or record does not describe.
tasks.altitude: Storage and security responsibility stays unchanged.

reach.task: Decide handling of drugs affected by abnormal storage conditions
reach.learn: Which observations require escalation under local procedures

evidence.claim: The design retains physical storage and security work and makes no automation saving claim.

assumptions: Boundary excludes clinical decisions on affected stock and equipment maintenance.
s1 produces the observed conditions used by s2; no structured excursion code or sensor feed is assumed.
Existing monitoring and pharmacist referral routes are unchanged, with no new workload transferred.
No new system or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Existing monitoring, storage layout and procedures
research_questions: Is there any separately measured duplicate logging burden outside physical storage maintenance?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+55=100. Inspection and physical maintenance remain unchanged, and incremental upkeep is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repetitive pharmacy record handling while retaining source checks and physical care.
role.ambitious_version: Maintain dependable records with visible uncertainty and unchanged clinical accountability.
